summary: EC is kept in the KeyPairGenerator allow-list against the literal api30 rule, with keySize 256
reason: generated/api30/KeyPairGenerator.cryptsl:45 declares alg in {"DSA","DH","RSA"} and then :53 declares alg in {"EC"} => keySize in {256}, a branch CrySL conjunctive CONSTRAINTS make unreachable. This is a MetaCrySL modelling defect, not intent: samples/jca/android/11plus/KeyPairGenerator.ref:2 writes define algorithm = {"EC"}; -- the command that fills a ${algorithm} hole -- but samples/jca/base/KeyPairGenerator.cryptsl:27 writes the list as a literal (alg in {"DH","DSA","RSA"};) instead of alg in ${algorithm}, so the define is discarded in silence. The same tier uses the same idiom in KeyGenerator.ref and it works, because samples/jca/base/KeyGenerator.cryptsl:27 does have the hole; only three base specifications fix the list literally (KeyManagerFactory, KeyPairGenerator, TrustManagerFactory) and only KeyPairGenerator has an Android .ref trying to extend it. EC is already in the seed (jca/KeyPairGeneratorSpec.mop:22, validate at :34), so this is a hunk kept against the rule, not an addition. The root fix is alg in ${algorithm} in the base specification and is NOT executed here, because MetaCrySL is not modified by this change. Justification: EC is the algorithm Android documents for AndroidKeyStore keys, so a literal transcription would fabricate exactly the class of spec-artefact this change exists to remove.

summary: SHA1withECDSA, SHA256withECDSA, SHA384withECDSA and SHA512withECDSA are added to the Signature allow-list
reason: generated/api30/Signature.cryptsl:75 lists twenty algorithms and exactly one ECDSA among them, SHA224withECDSA, because the only MetaCrySL tier that touches ECDSA is 20plus and it names that one; the others were never modelled. That the four exist on API 30 is read off the platform rather than inferred: Conscrypt android11-release registers Alg.Alias.Signature entries whose targets are those names -- OpenSSLProvider.java:270 (ECDSA) and :271 (ECDSAwithSHA1) point at SHA1withECDSA, :286 (SHA256/ECDSA) at SHA256withECDSA, :293 (SHA384/ECDSA) at SHA384withECDSA and :300 (SHA512/ECDSA) at SHA512withECDSA -- and a provider does not register an alias to a service it does not implement. The root fix is in MetaCrySL and is NOT executed here. Justification: ECDSA is the signature family Android pairs with AndroidKeyStore EC keys (the divergence above), so rejecting SHA256withECDSA while accepting EC key generation would report a violation on the platform own recommended pairing; the frozen jca already accepted three of the four, so a literal transcription would make the successor accuse where its predecessor did not.
